close_reason: Not a bug: String is moved into StateChange.new_state; call sites pass fresh format!() strings. No redundant clones found.
description:
In kith-store, several internal emit() methods take String by value but only use it to construct a StateChange:

- kith-store/src/contact.rs:23: fn emit(&self, new_state: String)
- kith-store/src/outbox.rs:44: fn emit(&self, new_state: String)
- kith-store/src/message.rs:646: fn emit(&self, new_state: String)
- kith-store/src/chat.rs:178: fn emit(&self, new_state: String)

StateChange has a new_state: String field, so the String is ultimately moved in. However, the call sites pass owned Strings constructed specifically for this call (e.g. format!("s-{}", counter)). The parameter type is fine for call sites that already have a String.

This is a minor issue — the type is correct (String is moved into StateChange.new_state). However, if any call site has to .clone() a string to pass it here, that would be wasteful. A quick audit of call sites to confirm no redundant clones would close this.
title: emit() takes String param where &str would suffice in kith-store
